The test image shows dense white/cottony mycelium with small round yellowish sclerotia at a stem/crown area — classic signs of a soilborne fungal disease. Top candidates: **Southern_Blight** (Sclerotium rolfsii — small round mustard-seed sclerotia) and **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (larger irregular sclerotia).

Let me view reference images for these two first, then explore other classes.
This Southern_Blight Bugwood_23 shows the same small round tan sclerotia on stem with white mycelium — very similar pattern to test image. Let me check a couple more classes to rule out alternatives.
I have 1 reference view remaining. Let me check one more class for coverage.

**Summary of visual analysis:**

- **Test image**: Dense white/fluffy cottony mycelium at stem base/crown with numerous small (~1-2mm), round, yellowish-tan sclerotia — classic "mustard seed" sclerotia
- **Southern_Blight (Bugwood_23)**: Matches closely — same small round tan sclerotia on stem with white mycelium; BugwoodIDs 5 and 13 were field views showing plant collapse
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot (Bugwood_14, 23)**: White mycelium present but sclerotia are clearly larger and dark/black — distinctly different from the small yellowish spheres in the test image
- **Gray_Mold, Rhizopus_Soft_Rots**: No cottony mycelium/sclerotia pattern; clearly different

The small, uniform, yellowish round sclerotia (~1-2mm, mustard-seed-like) in dense white cottony mycelium at the stem base is the definitive visual hallmark of *Sclerotium rolfsii* (Southern Blight).
